name: GhostCursor-TS-TW

frames.best_why: Frame 3 has the largest, brightest glow cloud with its trail and the cursor both visible.

tagline: A smoky violet halo drifts after the pointer, then fades.
summary: A soft cloud of lilac light chases the mouse across a dark panel, smearing into a blurry trail on fast moves and dimming out when the pointer stops.
appearance: A hazy lilac glow with a bright core and cloud-like edges floats over a near-black panel. It leaves faint smoke where the pointer has been, while the demo copy sits in the middle.
behaviour: The glow springs toward the pointer and trails a chain of earlier positions behind it, so quick moves leave a curved smear. When the pointer rests or leaves, it coasts, fades over a couple of seconds and stops.
demo_content: Heading "Move your cursor" and caption "A ghostly trail follows your pointer".
search_phrases: purple smoke that follows the mouse
soft light trail on pointer move
ethereal trail for a dark landing page
shader smoke trail around the cursor
use_when: A dark, atmospheric page wants a luminescent cursor trail for drama.
avoid_when: The glowing cloud hides text it passes over, and the WebGL layer costs real GPU time on every move.
customise: Trail length, inertia, grain, bloom strength and radius, brightness, colour, blend mode, edge fade, resolution cap and z-index are props. There is no content.
weight_why: A WebGL shader with bloom and film grain runs a full post-processing chain every frame.

a11y.note: No content or controls, but the WebGL glow and grain ignore reduced-motion and can strain low-power devices.

issues: The glow washes out the centre heading when the pointer crosses it.
There is no reduced-motion path and the full-screen WebGL pass can tax weaker devices.
polish_why: Convincing smoky light and a natural fade; the trail can bury nearby copy.
title: Ghost Cursor Trail
